Unauthorized.description: Missing or wrong Basic Auth credentials.

WWW-Authenticate.description: `Basic realm="featherbit admin"` — omitted when the request carries `X-Featherbit-Client` (the web UI), so browsers don't open their native login dialog.

certs.description: Every managed certificate, sorted by id; empty when disabled.

storage.description:
Where certificates are persisted, e.g. `filesystem`; omitted when
`enabled` is false.

AcmeCertStatus.description: One managed certificate. Never includes key material.

id.description:
Certificate id: its normalized (lowercased, sorted, deduplicated)
domain list, comma-separated.

last_attempt_at.description: When issuance/renewal was last attempted, Unix seconds.

last_error.description: Why the last attempt failed, if it did.

next_renewal_at.description: When the next renewal is due, Unix seconds.

not_after.description: Validity end, Unix seconds; `0` for a placeholder.

not_before.description: Validity start, Unix seconds; `0` for a placeholder.

purged.description:
What the backends purged before the failure (`cache_purge_failed`
only).

CachePurgeResult.description: Successful response body: the purged id and what each backend reported.

purged.description: One entry per distinct backend holding the pair.

credentials.description:
Per-auth-plugin credentials, keyed by plugin type
(e.g. `key-auth: {key}`, `basic-auth: {username, password}`).

labels.description:
Free-form labels; `custom_id` is special-cased into the
`X-Consumer-Custom-ID` header (matching APISIX).

name.description: Unique consumer name (the identity attached to matching requests).

DebugSettings.description: Body of `GET /api/debug/config`: the effective debug settings.

capture_bodies.description: Whether request/response bodies are captured in snapshots.

max_steps.description: Per-trace cap on recorded node steps.

trace_all.description: Whether every request is traced, header or not.

trigger_header.description: Request header that opts a request into tracing (lowercased).

retention.description:
What the ring buffer holds and has evicted, so an empty `traces` can
be told apart from a rotated-out match.

EdgeConfig.description:
A directed edge between two node ports, written as `node_id.port`.

Ports: `out`, `success`, `error` on the source side; `in` on the target
side (e.g. `from: auth.success`, `to: upstream.in`).

names.description:
Names of the process's environment variables, sorted. Values are never
exposed.

ErrorResponse.description:
`{"error": "..."}` — the body of every 4xx/5xx the admin API produces
itself.

error.description: Human-readable reason, or a short code such as `not_found`.

GatewayConfig.description:
Root of `gateway.yaml`: the route table and the policies it references.

Both sections default to empty, so a missing or minimal file is valid.

```yaml
routes:
  - name: api
    match: { path: /api/* }
    policy: api-policy
policies:
  - name: api-policy
    nodes:
      - { id: in, type: listener }
      - { id: up, type: upstream, config: { url: "http://backend:3000" } }
    edges:
      - { from: in.out, to: up.in }
```

consumers.description:
Named API clients with per-auth-plugin credentials; resolved by auth
nodes configured with `use_consumers: true`.

plugin_configs.description:
Named, typed plugin configurations shared by any number of plugin
nodes via `config_ref`; resolved at compile time (src/config/resolve.rs).

routes.description: Routes evaluated in declaration order; the first match wins.

stores.description:
Named shared stores (redis/valkey connections) referenced by plugin
config (`store: <name>`); clients are built at config-apply time
(src/stores/), so `${ENV_VAR}` placeholders never leave this struct
resolved.

supernodes.description:
Reusable named subgraphs, referenced from policies by nodes of
`type: supernode`; inlined at compile time (see src/graph/expand.rs).

MatchRule.description:
Request-matching conditions for a route.

All specified criteria must match (logical AND); every field defaults to
unset/empty, which matches any request.

headers.description: Required header name → value pairs; empty means no header constraints.

host.description:
Required `Host` value; `None` matches any host. Exact hostname or a
single-label wildcard (`*.example.com`); the request's port is ignored.
Merged with [`hosts`](Self::hosts) at match time.

hosts.description:
Additional accepted `Host` patterns (same syntax as `host`); the route
matches when any entry matches. Empty means no constraint beyond `host`.

methods.description: Allowed HTTP methods; empty means any method.

path.description: Path pattern to match (e.g. `/api/*`); `None` matches any path.

McpPromptArgument.description: One argument of a precompiled prompt.

name.description: Argument name (the query parameter name when rendering).

McpPromptError.description: Error body of `GET /api/mcp/prompts/{name}` for everything but `404`.

hint.description: What to do about it, when there is a suggestion.

McpPromptInfo.description: One precompiled prompt and its arguments.

arguments.description: Arguments, passed as query parameters when rendering.

description.description: What the prompt asks the agent to do.

McpStatus.description: Body of `GET /api/mcp/status`. Never carries token values.

compiled.description: Whether the binary was built with the `mcp` cargo feature.

enabled.description: Whether the MCP endpoint is served (compiled in and `admin.mcp.enabled`).

path.description: Mount path on the admin listener (`admin.mcp.path`, default `/mcp`).

scopes.description: Distinct scopes (`read`/`write`) granted by those tokens, sorted.

NodeConfig.description: One plugin node in a policy graph.

config.description: Free-form plugin-specific configuration; defaults to empty.

config_ref.description:
Optional name of a shared [`PluginConfigDef`] to inherit configuration
from. The effective config is the shared config with this node's own
`config` keys layered on top (shallow merge, local wins), materialized
at compile time — the stored form always keeps the reference.

id.description: Unique node id within the policy, referenced by edges as `id.port`.

position.description:
Canvas coordinates for the Web UI node editor; ignored by the engine
and omitted from serialized output when unset.

type.description:
Plugin type (YAML key: `type`), e.g. `upstream`, `key-auth`, `script`;
must be one of the registered plugin types.

plugins.description: Every registered node type, in reference-docs category order.

PluginConfigDef.description:
A named, shared plugin configuration, referenced by plugin nodes of the
matching type via [`NodeConfig::config_ref`]. Editing a shared config
re-resolves and recompiles every referencing policy atomically.

config.description: The shared plugin configuration; same shape as [`NodeConfig::config`].

description.description: Optional human-readable description (shown in the UI library).

type.description:
Plugin type this config is for (YAML key: `type`); only nodes of the
same type may reference it.

description.description: What leaving on this port means.

PluginPortKind.description: The flavor of an output port (mirrors `plugins::ports::PortKind`).

input.description:
Description of the single `in` port; `null` when the node has no
input (only `listener`).

outputs.description: Declared output ports, in declaration order.

PluginTypeInfo.description:
One node type in the catalog. Documents the shape of the entries
`plugin_catalog()` builds.

type.description: Node type id, as used in a policy node's `type`.

PolicyBufferingNotice.description:
An upstream that must buffer its response instead of streaming it.
Documents the shape of the graph engine's `BufferingReason`.

blocked_by.description: Id of the downstream node that forces buffering.

upstream.description: Id of the `upstream` node that cannot stream.

PolicyCachePairNotice.description:
One half of a `proxy-cache` lookup/store pair with no counterpart.
Documents the shape of the graph engine's `CachePairWarning`.

cache_id.description: The shared cache `id` that links a pair.

missing_role.description: The half that is missing: `lookup` or `store`.

present_node_id.description: Id of the node (the half) that is present.

PolicyConfig.description:
A node-graph policy: a named pipeline of plugin nodes wired by edges.

Compiled into a `CompiledGraph` at load/reload time; execution starts at
the `listener` node and follows each node's `success`/`error` ports.

error_handler.description: Optional id of a node to jump to when a node errors without an explicit error edge.

nodes.description: Plugin nodes making up the pipeline.

buffering.description:
Upstreams forced to buffer instead of stream, and the node responsible.
Informational. Empty when the policy is invalid.

cache_pairs.description:
`proxy-cache` halves (lookup or store) with no counterpart. Informational.
Empty when the policy is invalid; absent when the body does not
deserialize as a policy at all.

errors.description: Compilation errors, one per entry; empty when `valid`.

valid.description:
Whether the policy compiles. Buffering and cache-pair notices do not
make it invalid.

Position.description: 2D canvas coordinates of a node in the Web UI graph editor.

PurgeOutcome.description: What one backend reported after a purge.

removed.description: How many cached entries were removed.

store.description: The declared store's name; omitted for `local`.

acme.description: ACME certificate readiness; present in every branch.

reason.description:
Why the gateway is not ready (`no routes loaded`, `acme starting` or
`acme placeholder certs`); absent when ready.

routes.description: Number of compiled routes; present only when ready.

placeholder.description:
Ids of ACME-managed certificates still serving a placeholder (never
successfully issued). Empty when ready.

description.description: What the prompt asks the agent to do.

text.description:
The rendered prompt text (one user message), byte-identical to MCP
`prompts/get`.

RouteConfig.description: Binds a request match rule to a named policy.

match.description: Conditions a request must satisfy (YAML key: `match`).

name.description: Unique route name, used in logs, metrics labels, and the Admin API.

policy.description: Name of the [`PolicyConfig`] to execute; must exist or compilation fails.

RouteOrder.description:
Body of `PUT /api/routes`: every existing route name, exactly once, in the
new evaluation order.

SandboxOnError.description: What to do when an ad-hoc node fails.

SandboxRequest.description:
A sandbox request: exactly one of `nodes` or `policy`.

`context` is taken as a raw value and normalised by [`materialize_context`],
so it accepts **both** the flat hand-authored shape *and* a context copied
straight out of a trace (the nested `{request, response, message, errors}`
snapshot shape). Typos in the flat shape are still rejected — validation
runs after normalisation.

context.description:
Synthetic request context: the flat input shape, or a context copied
from a trace. Omitted or `null` yields a plain `GET /`.

nodes.description:
Ad-hoc node list, chained in order between an implicit `listener`
and `client`. Mutually exclusive with `policy`.

on_error.description: How a failing ad-hoc node is wired (ignored in `policy` mode).

policy.description: Name of a stored policy to run. Mutually exclusive with `nodes`.
The policy executed (`__sandbox` for ad-hoc node lists).

stored_trace_id.description: Id of the trace stored in the debug ring buffer.

trace.description: The rendered trace, same shape as `GET /api/debug/traces/{id}`.

warning.description: Reminder that plugins ran for real.

SandboxTimeoutError.description: Body of the `504` a sandbox run returns when it times out.

ScriptFile.description: A scripted-plugin file found on disk.

file.description: Path of the file, as the gateway sees it.

runtime.description: Scripting runtime, derived from the extension (currently always `lua`).

scripts.description: Every recognized script file in the `plugins/` directory.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; `null` on the last page.

sessions.description: Session metadata; payloads never leave the store.

SessionMeta.description:
Unencrypted envelope for the operator surface. `id` is left empty on
`put` (the key already carries it) and filled in by `list`.

plugin.description: Node type that established the session, e.g. `openid-connect`.

policy.description: Policy the session was established under.

route.description: Route the session was established on.

subject.description:
Authenticated subject; may be empty (e.g. an opaque token with no
decodable claims) — such sessions are not indexed by subject.

default_credentials.description:
Whether the admin API still accepts the shipped default credentials
(the UI warns while it does).

StoreConfig.description:
A named shared store: a redis/valkey connection referenced by name from
plugin config. Declared under top-level `stores:`. `url` and `password`
support `${ENV_VAR:-default}` placeholders, resolved only when the client
is built — the stored config (and everything the Admin API serves) keeps
the raw placeholder.

connect_budget_ms.description:
Total budget for establishing the first connection, covering every
retry and the backoff between them.

`connect_timeout_ms` bounds one attempt only, so without this the
connection manager's retry schedule decides how long a request waits
on an unreachable store -- tens of seconds with the crate defaults, on
the first request after an outage begins. A failed connect is not
cached, so the next request tries again.

connect_timeout_ms.description:
Connect/response timeout applied to the client and to `ping`. Bounds a
single attempt; see `connect_budget_ms` for the total.

description.description: Optional human-readable description (shown in the UI library).

key_prefix.description: Namespace prefix for every key this store writes.

name.description: Unique name, referenced by plugin config (`store: <name>`).

password.description: Optional password; overrides any password embedded in `url`.

topology.description:
Reserved for HA topologies (`sentinel`/`cluster`); v1 accepts only
`standalone` (the default) and rejects anything else at config load.

type.description:
Backend type (YAML key: `type`): `redis` or `valkey` — aliases for the
same RESP backend.

urls.description:
Reserved for HA topologies (sentinel/cluster endpoint lists); rejected
at config load in v1.

StoreInUse.description:
`409` body of `DELETE /api/stores/{name}` when the store is still
referenced.

StorePingResult.description:
`200` body of `POST /api/stores/{name}/ping`. Never echoes the resolved
connection details.

latency_ms.description: Round-trip time of the `PING`, in milliseconds.

message.description: Which bound elapsed, e.g. `no reply within connect_timeout_ms (2000ms)`.

ca_cert_path.description: PEM CA bundle for a private CA.

SupernodeConfig.description:
A reusable named subgraph with a boundary of one `input`, one or more
`output`, and one or more `error` pseudo-nodes; each output/error node's
id is an instance port name (`output` = the `success` port; `error` =
the default error port) (declared in `nodes` like a policy declares
`listener`/`client`, so the UI can persist positions).

Instances appear in policies as nodes of `type: supernode` with
`config: { name: <this name> }` and are inlined at compile time —
stored configuration always keeps the compact reference form.

description.description: Optional human-readable description (shown in the UI library).

edges.description:
Directed connections; boundary edges use `input.out`, `output.in`,
`error.in` endpoints.

name.description: Unique supernode name, referenced from policy nodes' `config.name`.

nodes.description:
Inner plugin nodes plus the boundary pseudo-nodes: one `input`, one
or more `output`, and one or more `error` pseudo-nodes; each
output/error node's id is an instance port name (`output` = the
`success` port; `error` = the default error port).

TraceRetention.description: What the ring buffer currently holds, and what it has thrown away.

oldest_seq.description:
`seq` of the oldest trace still held; `None` when the buffer is empty.
Anything older than this is gone.

truncated.description:
Whether anything has been evicted at all. When true, an empty result
may mean "rotated out", not "never happened".

TraceSource.description: Whether a trace came from live traffic or a sandbox run.

TraceSummary.description: Row shape for the trace list view.

error_count.description: Steps that exited through an error.

route.description: Matched route; absent for sandbox runs.

source.description: Live traffic or a sandbox run.

vars.description: Every variable the resolver accepts, statics first, then families.

VarEntry.description:
One catalog row. `family_source` names the context collection that
populates a family's live suggestions in the UI.

family_source.description: For a family, the context collection that supplies its members.

name.description: Variable name without the `$`; families end in `*` (e.g. `http_*`).

path.description:
Template path equivalent for the universal-templates feature.
Empty string means no direct template mapping (e.g., protocol, query_string, post_arg_*).

VarKind.description: Whether an entry is a fixed name or a `prefix_*` family.

info.description:
REST API of the featherbit gateway's admin listener: CRUD for routes, policies, supernodes, plugin configs, consumers and stores; server-side sessions; ACME certificates; debug traces and the plugin sandbox; status, health and metrics.

All endpoints require HTTP Basic authentication except `/healthz` and `/readyz`. The MCP endpoint (`admin.mcp.path`, default `/mcp`) is a Streamable HTTP MCP transport with its own bearer tokens and is not described here.
info.title: featherbit Admin API

get.description:
Deliberately **not** gated: it returns only booleans the UI needs to explain
itself, and answering it is what turns "the button does nothing" into "debug
mode is off, here is the key to set".

200.description: The effective debug settings; answers even while debug mode is off.

post.description:
Plugins execute **for real**: outbound callouts are made, rate-limit
counters decrement, breakers trip, loggers fire. That is the point (a
`key-auth` node that did not resolve real consumers would be a lie), but it
is why the endpoint is gated behind `debug.enabled` + `debug.sandbox` on top
of admin auth, and why every response carries a `warning`.

Errors: `400` for a malformed request or a plugin config the compiler
rejects; `404` for an unknown policy; `504` if the run exceeds
`debug.sandbox_timeout_seconds`.

200.description: The run completed; its trace is inlined and stored. Plugins executed for real.

400.description: Malformed request (both or neither of `nodes`/`policy`, a bad node list or plugin config, an invalid policy, or an unmaterializable `context`), or an unparseable JSON body.

404.description: Debug mode or the sandbox is off (`error: not_found`), or `policy` names no stored policy.

fails if a registered type is missing.

Response: `{"valid": bool, "errors": [...], "buffering": [...]}`. A
policy that forces one or more upstreams to buffer instead of stream is
still `valid` — `buffering` is informational, not an error. Each entry
names the blocked upstream and the node responsible:
`{"upstream": "up", "blocked_by": "rw", "node_type": "response-rewrite"}`.
`cache_pairs` likewise lists unpaired `proxy-cache` halves; it is omitted
when the body does not even parse as a policy.

get.description:
Ready means the route table is loaded, the ACME runtime exists when
`system.yaml` asks for managed certificates, **and** no ACME-managed
certificate is still serving a placeholder — renewal failures never affect
readiness, only a cert that has never successfully issued does. Returns `200 OK` with
the compiled route count (and the empty `acme.placeholder` list) once
both hold, or `503 Service Unavailable` while either does not. Every
branch carries the same `acme.placeholder` shape, even "no routes loaded"
(where the acme runtime hasn't necessarily been consulted), so callers
can rely on one JSON shape regardless of why readiness failed.

200.description: Ready (`status: ready`, with the compiled route count).

503.description: Not ready (`status: not_ready`, with a `reason`): no routes loaded, the ACME runtime is still starting, or a managed certificate is still a placeholder.
